concepts.title: Turn answer comparisons into a policy update
concepts.meaning: DPO optimizes the chosen-versus-rejected policy/reference log-probability margin using a preference-classification loss.
concepts.brief: Keep the prompt fixed. Show chosen and rejected answers, compute each policy/reference log-probability ratio, subtract to obtain the DPO margin, then update the two response likelihoods with the reference anchor visible.
pitfalls: Do not imply DPO is an online reward-model loop.
DPO and PPO can produce different checkpoints; compare the resulting policies on the same evaluation.
Shared parameters can lower both absolute sequence probabilities while improving the relative margin.

concepts.title: A verifier turns an answer into a training signal
concepts.meaning: A defined checker evaluates a testable property of a generated answer and supplies an outcome reward to reinforcement learning.
concepts.brief: Show a natural-language math or code task, the generated candidate, the executable or symbolic check, and its binary outcome. Sample a group of candidate answers and compute relative advantages from actual verifier scores.
pitfalls: A verifier can only check the contract it implements.
Formatting success alone does not establish correctness.
Subjective qualities need a different evaluation signal.

concepts.title: Balance domain adaptation with replay
concepts.meaning: Continued pretraining changes a language model through next-token prediction on new domain text, while replay assigns some scored targets to general data.
concepts.brief: Mix domain and replay targets in a fixed token budget. Show the resulting weighted gradient on a shared parameter, then compare domain and general evaluation lanes across candidate checkpoints.
pitfalls: Choose replay ratios through domain and general-task evaluation under the intended token budget.
A token mixture matches the intended objective only when scored-token weighting is correct.
Lower domain perplexity alone does not establish a better downstream model.

concepts.title: Shard training memory and gather each compute unit
concepts.meaning: ZeRO and FSDP reduce replicated training state by partitioning optimizer state, gradients, and parameters across data-parallel ranks.
concepts.brief: Start with replicated weight, gradient, and optimizer slots on four training ranks. Reveal ZeRO stages as successive shards; animate FSDP parameter all-gather before a wrapped unit and gradient reduce-scatter after backward.
pitfalls: The ledger excludes activation memory and temporary communication buffers unless shown.
Full sharding trades memory for collectives and depends on unit wrapping and topology.
Training-state sharding differs from inference tensor parallelism.

concepts.title: Interpolate compatible model weights and test the path
concepts.meaning: Weight interpolation combines aligned parameter tensors; its quality depends on whether the checkpoints occupy compatible regions of parameter space.
concepts.brief: Display matching tensors from models fine-tuned from the same base, calculate a weighted midpoint, and trace held-out loss along the interpolation path. Contrast with a one-dimensional double-well example where averaging across separated minima raises loss.
pitfalls: Parameter names and tensor shapes do not prove neuron alignment.
Averaging unrelated independently initialized checkpoints can fail.
Evaluate real merged checkpoints on held-out tasks after checking the toy interpolation.

concepts.title: Bound each record before adding calibrated noise
concepts.meaning: DP-SGD clips each protected-unit contribution, aggregates them, adds calibrated Gaussian noise, and composes privacy cost across training steps.
concepts.brief: Use two-dimensional record gradients with a visible L2 clip circle. Shorten outliers to the boundary, sum the clipped vectors, animate a Gaussian perturbation, then connect sampling rate, noise multiplier, step count, adjacency, and delta to an accountant.
pitfalls: Per-batch-average clipping does not imply the same sensitivity bound as per-record clipping.
One realized noisy update does not establish a DP guarantee.
Epsilon depends on the protected unit, adjacency, sampler, noise, and all composed releases.

concepts.title: Build a filtered dataset from generated examples
concepts.meaning: Synthetic training data requires a declared source process, task coverage, independent checks, admission rules, and downstream evaluation.
concepts.brief: Seed a small natural-language task set, generate variants, execute arithmetic or code checks where possible, filter duplicates and invalid candidates, then visualize admitted coverage and a held-out downstream result.
pitfalls: A fluent generation can still be false or underspecified.
A judge must be calibrated and independently audited for the task.
Recursive training can amplify generator errors and narrow the data distribution.

concepts.title: Turn written principles into critique, revision, and feedback
concepts.meaning: Constitutional AI uses written principles to condition self-critique and revision, then can train from AI-generated preference comparisons.
concepts.brief: Keep one request and policy boundary fixed. Animate a draft, a principle-specific critique, and a revised supervised target; then show a separate AI preference comparison and reward-learning phase. End with a red-team case and independent human audit.
pitfalls: The principle does not replace application authorization or access controls.
The critique is training scaffolding; the revised answer is the direct-answer supervised target.
AI feedback can share the model family’s blind spots and needs external evaluation.

concepts.title: Dataset lineage gates
concepts.meaning: A source record passes through schema, identity, and group checks before a versioned dataset is released.
concepts.brief: Animate support records through schema and label checks, exact normalized fingerprints, conflict quarantine, group-level splits, near-duplicate candidate review, benchmark checks, privacy decisions, and a manifest. Keep exact identity distinct from semantic similarity; make open reviews and digest trust boundaries visible.
pitfalls: Do not treat exact hashes as semantic similarity or digest consistency as publisher authentication.
Do not split related conversation or incident records across held-out partitions.
LSH returns probabilistic candidates; keep its assumptions and review policy visible.
A scan result covers only its declared patterns and source snapshot.

concepts.title: Feature contract vector
concepts.meaning: Named measurements pass through type and availability checks into fixed ordered model coordinates.
concepts.brief: Build the 09:00 J-204 prediction row from event and availability clocks, then show fitted numeric transforms, missingness indicators, categorical encoding, a fixed feature order, a preprocessing edit, and offline/serving parity. Keep illustrative coefficients and thresholds labeled as authored examples.
pitfalls: Exclude future events and labels even when present in today's backfill.
Robust scaling does not clip outliers.
Smoothing does not replace out-of-fold or time-aware target encoding.
Preprocessing changes affect only inputs they actually alter; measure the paired model behavior.

concepts.title: Recommendation candidate slate
concepts.meaning: Eligible candidates are retrieved, scored, and assembled into an ordered recommendation slate.
concepts.brief: Filter stale or unauthorized documents, move a seven-item retrieval shortlist through a hand-authored scorer, compare ranked lists and graded gains, then apply slate constraints. Keep candidate recall separate from reranking quality, policy eligibility, and online causal measurement.
pitfalls: A ranker cannot recover a relevant item omitted from candidate generation.
Learned relevance scores never grant access to private content.
Illustrative fixture scores and funnel counts are not benchmark measurements.
Position-biased clicks and offline ranking metrics do not by themselves establish online product impact.

concepts.title: Forecast residual band
concepts.meaning: A forecast center and uncertainty band are compared with observed values and their residuals.
concepts.brief: Animate a timestamped demand fixture across a rolling forecast origin, update the baseline and forecast interval, reveal residuals only after observations arrive, and compare anomaly thresholds with normal seasonal variation. Label authored values as illustrative and preserve future-data boundaries.
pitfalls: Forecasts use information available at their origin; later observations belong to scoring the forecast.
Residual alarms require seasonality, horizon, and uncertainty context.
Prediction intervals express uncertainty under a model and data regime; they are not guaranteed bounds.
Keep illustrative fixtures distinct from measured forecast performance.

concepts.title: Model monitoring drift
concepts.meaning: Reference and current feature distributions are compared as a monitored shift is surfaced for review.
concepts.brief: Follow a deployed model from stable feature distributions through an input shift, delayed labels, outcome metrics, and a canary decision. Separate feature drift, prediction drift, data quality, and delayed outcome evidence; compare to a fixed reference and show uncertainty before rollback decisions.
pitfalls: Feature drift is a review signal, not proof of model degradation.
Without labels, outcome quality may be delayed or unavailable.
A single aggregate metric can hide segment failures and changing traffic mix.
Rollback or retraining thresholds need explicit operational evidence and ownership.

concepts.title: Serving benchmark latency
concepts.meaning: A measured serving trace separates median latency from the slower tail over a defined load interval.
concepts.brief: Grow concurrent requests against a model server, animate queue depth and token throughput, and update latency percentiles from the same authored request trace. Contrast steady-state and overload, include warmup and request length, and keep local fixture values explicitly illustrative.
pitfalls: Throughput, time to first token, inter-token latency, and end-to-end latency answer different questions.
Averages can hide tail latency; report the percentile with its sample and workload definition.
Do not present authored example timings as hardware benchmark results.
Warmup, concurrency, prompt/output lengths, batching, and error rates affect comparisons.

concepts.title: Token economics meter
concepts.meaning: Input, cached context, and generated output have separate token usage and cost weights.
concepts.brief: Trace a request's prompt, reusable cached prefix, generated output, retries, and tool steps into token and dollar cost; compute cost per successful task from an explicitly authored workload. Show how routing, batching, context trimming, and cache reuse change both cost and quality constraints.
pitfalls: Provider prices and cache discounts vary and change; cite a dated source or use clearly authored example rates.
Tokens are not words, and input, cached input, and generated output may be billed differently.
Cost per request omits retries, failures, and task success; state the denominator.
Savings must be evaluated with quality, latency, and provider-specific behavior held visible.

concepts.title: Testing a paired model comparison
concepts.meaning: The paired task is the analysis unit. A null model over disagreement signs gives an exact tail probability, while intervals describe effect-size uncertainty.
concepts.brief: Keep each prompt, both model outcomes, and the shared hidden tests in one row. Show five ties and one B-only win, then condition on disagreement count and animate fair-coin outcomes under the null. Compare the exact one-sided tail for one of one and thirteen of sixteen wins. Continue to false-positive and missed-improvement decisions, the search cost of twenty comparisons, paired-row bootstrap lift, and a separate pass-at-k candidate budget.
pitfalls: A p-value is a tail probability under the null, not the probability that the null is true.
Ties contribute to pass rates and lift but not the conditional sign-test win count.
The test direction and comparison family must be declared before looking at results.
Bootstrap resample frequency is not a null p-value.
Prompt variants and repeated tasks can violate independent-task assumptions.

concepts.title: Estimating the causal effect of a randomized change
concepts.meaning: Random assignment supports a causal comparison when treatment is well-defined, assignment is preserved, outcomes are measured consistently, and interference is controlled.
concepts.brief: Randomly assign users to control and treatment, show equal expected baselines and the observed click-through rates, then calculate risk difference, relative lift, standard error, and a confidence interval from the same counts. Reveal allocation ratio and guardrail metrics, then demonstrate how sample-ratio mismatch, repeated peeking, contamination, and noncompliance change the claim. Separate an intention-to-treat estimate from a per-protocol comparison.
pitfalls: Randomization balances measured and unmeasured baseline causes only in expectation.
A treatment effect is tied to the assigned intervention and target population.
Repeated unplanned peeking can inflate error unless a sequential design is used.
Sample-ratio mismatch is a diagnostic signal that needs investigation, not a causal effect.
Statistical significance does not establish product value or rule out guardrail harm.

concepts.title: Learning a policy from state, action, and reward
concepts.meaning: A policy maps observed states to actions whose consequences produce rewards and later states under a specified decision process.
concepts.brief: Use a small stochastic navigation fixture with explicit states, actions, transition probabilities, rewards, terminal states, and discount factor. Compare a one-step bandit reward with a multi-step Markov decision process, animate a trajectory, then compute a Bellman backup and a Q-learning update from the realized transition. Show that exploration changes which evidence the agent collects and that a reward specification does not guarantee safe or useful behavior.
pitfalls: The Markov property applies to the modeled state; omitted history may make the chosen state representation insufficient.
A bandit action has no action-dependent next state in the basic formulation.
Model-free Q-learning's convergence results require specific finite tabular and exploration assumptions.
Discounting changes the objective and finite-horizon problems need terminal handling.
An optimized reward can diverge from the real objective.

concepts.title: Grouping observations and rotating to principal directions
concepts.meaning: Clustering assigns observations under a chosen distance and objective; PCA finds orthogonal directions of maximum centered variance.
concepts.brief: Generate a small anisotropic cloud with two visible groups, animate Lloyd assignment and centroid updates from fixed initial centers, and report inertia for the resulting partition. Then center the same points, compute covariance and a leading eigenvector, and rotate a unit-scaled coordinate frame to show projected variance and reconstruction error. Distinguish cluster labels from PCA coordinates, explain feature scaling and local optima, and note that PCA preserves variance rather than task relevance.
pitfalls: K-means minimizes within-cluster squared Euclidean distance and favors compact roughly spherical groups.
Results depend on initialization and feature scaling.
PCA centers data before computing principal directions.
Equal pixels per unit are required when the drawing represents Euclidean distances or angles.
High-variance directions need not preserve downstream predictive information.

concepts.title: Reading tensor shapes through array operations
concepts.meaning: Array axes encode which dimensions align, reduce, transpose, or broadcast during a computation.
concepts.brief: Build a tiny batch-by-token-by-feature tensor and track its shape through indexing, reduction, reshape, transpose, and broadcasting. Show each input's dimensions before an elementwise addition, align shapes from the trailing axes, and expand a size-one dimension across the compatible batch. Then reshape a toy attention tensor into batch, head, token, and head-width axes while preserving element counts. Use explicit axis labels and verify every displayed element from the numeric arrays.
pitfalls: Broadcasting compares dimensions from the right and permits equal sizes or a size of one.
A reduction removes the selected axis unless keepdims is requested.
Reshape preserves element order while transpose permutes axes.
Equal element counts do not imply that a reshape preserves semantic axis meaning.
Batch, token, head, and feature axes must be labeled consistently with the source operation.

concepts.title: Memory retention valve
concepts.meaning: Gates control how stored recurrent evidence survives and how a candidate enters the state.
concepts.brief: Follow an old-state amount through retention, addition, and exposure.
concepts.pitfalls: Keep cell and hidden state distinct, identify gate convention, and isolate the direct gradient path.

concepts.title: Latent posterior cloud
concepts.meaning: An encoder describes a distribution of possible latent codes for an observed input.
concepts.brief: Transform an independent noise point into a posterior sample and decode it.
concepts.pitfalls: Distinguish posterior from prior, standard deviation from variance, and reconstruction from sampling quality.

concepts.title: Selective affine scan
concepts.meaning: Input-dependent affine updates compose in order to recover every prefix state.
concepts.brief: Compute carry and write terms, regroup adjacent update pairs, and compare every state with the sequential reference.
concepts.pitfalls: Preserve update order, distinguish Mamba discretization from exact zero-order hold, and account for every live buffer.

concepts.title: Patch to token
concepts.meaning: A spatial pixel patch becomes a projected vector while its location remains separately represented.
concepts.brief: Follow raster-order patch values through a shared projection and position-aware attention, then count visual slots.
concepts.pitfalls: Keep patch count, raw width, hidden width, and bridge output count separate. Evaluate exact detail after preprocessing.

concepts.title: Feature centering
concepts.meaning: Per-token normalization centers and rescales feature coordinates before learned affine adjustments.
concepts.brief: Animate mean subtraction and variance scaling, then compare residual and gradient paths around normalization.
concepts.pitfalls: Keep reduction axes explicit, preserve epsilon, and avoid interpreting an identity path as a lower bound on the full gradient.

concepts.title: Sparse feature dictionary
concepts.meaning: A sparse code reconstructs a mixed model activation using a few learned dictionary directions.
concepts.brief: Build a known superposition, infer sparse coefficients, reconstruct it, and test a feature intervention.
concepts.pitfalls: Separate learned feature associations, reconstruction fidelity, and demonstrated causal effects. Control decoder scaling.

concepts.title: Reasoning budget tree
concepts.meaning: Inference budget can fund longer reasoning, more candidates, and verification before selecting an answer.
concepts.brief: Allocate a finite budget across candidate branches, show oracle availability versus selection accuracy, and stop under explicit cost.
concepts.pitfalls: Candidate independence, verifier mistakes, correlation, and latency affect the value of additional sampling.

concepts.title: Token surprisal
concepts.meaning: A model assigns log loss to observed tokens and perplexity exponentiates their average surprise.
concepts.brief: Compare token probability products through accumulated log loss, weighted corpus aggregation, and context-window scoring.
concepts.pitfalls: Match tokenization, target masking, context policy, and evaluation data before comparing perplexities.

concepts.title: Turn a page into traceable evidence
concepts.meaning: Format-specific extraction produces candidate text; page location, parser route, quality review, and checksum make an admitted record inspectable.
concepts.brief: Carry the rollback rule from a PDF page through native extraction or OCR review into a locatable record. Show why 15 becoming 1S must pause for review, preserve table row and unit structure, and carry source identity through chunking.
pitfalls: Treating a long OCR extract as proof that a critical value was recognized correctly
Detaching a number from its table row, unit, condition, or qualifier
Dropping source locators during chunking
Treating a checksum as proof of source authenticity or extraction fidelity

concepts.title: Let evidence inform the answer without granting authority
concepts.meaning: Retrieved or user-supplied text can influence model output, while deterministic host policy controls credentials, disclosure, and side effects.
concepts.brief: Follow an evaluation report that contains a factual result and an injected deployment command. Keep source labels visible, let the model propose text or a typed action, then show the application checking identity, capability, arguments, and approval before any protected sink.
pitfalls: Treating XML tags, role labels, or repeated reminders as a security boundary
Describing prompt injection as a text pattern that a perfect classifier can remove
Assuming the injected command has authority because the application fetched its source
Confusing a helpful refusal with a blocked unauthorized side effect

concepts.title: Reduce and scan with real synchronization boundaries
concepts.meaning: A reduction combines values into one result, while a prefix scan produces a result for each position; parallel groups need explicit communication and barriers.
concepts.brief: Compute a small vector sum first, then animate warp-level pairwise shuffle steps and block partials with barriers. Compare a prefix scan that exposes every cumulative total, show floating-point tree order, and update online softmax's running maximum and rescaled sum from computed state.
pitfalls: Showing a reduction tree without calculating each intermediate value
Using warp shuffle as if it were a memory barrier
Implying blocks in an ordinary kernel can synchronize globally at an arbitrary point
Treating floating-point reassociation as exact real arithmetic
Describing Hillis-Steele and Blelloch scans without showing work and output contracts

concepts.title: Move request state from prefill to decode
concepts.meaning: A disaggregated inference path schedules a request, computes prompt KV state, transfers compatible state, and then generates output tokens on a decode worker.
concepts.brief: Trace one request's ownership and KV blocks from prefill to decode. Compute payload bytes from token, layer, head, and dtype dimensions; reserve destination capacity before transfer, validate matching model/layout metadata, and separate transport completion from request execution and client delivery.
pitfalls: Treating a transfer engine as the owner of a request or its retry policy
Assuming all state layouts or worker versions are interchangeable
Counting enqueue as transfer completion or transfer completion as a generated response
Retrying an uncertain transfer or downstream action without an operation identity and reconciliation

concepts.title: Measure whether an automated judge tracks human review
concepts.meaning: An LLM judge applies a defined rubric to controlled candidates, while randomized order swaps, human labels, agreement measures, uncertainty, and coverage checks evaluate the judge itself.
concepts.brief: Show an explicit pairwise rubric, swap A/B order while keeping candidate text fixed, compare blinded human judgments, and compute disagreement, coverage, and agreement on an illustrative labeled fixture. Separate bias probes from validity and report the reviewed denominator.
pitfalls: Treating a judge score as independent proof of answer quality
Calling order sensitivity a universal fixed preference direction
Reporting agreement without the eligible reviewed denominator
Using accuracy alone when class imbalance or abstentions matter

concepts.title: Coordinate a live voice turn through interruption
concepts.meaning: Streaming speech recognition, turn commitment, response generation, synthesis, transport, playback acknowledgement, and barge-in cancellation are distinct events on overlapping clocks.
concepts.brief: Use an explicitly synthetic incident-hotline trace: stream STT while the caller speaks, commit only after a complete stable identifier, overlap LLM and TTS work, then cancel queued playback on barge-in. Track which audio the client acknowledged separately from generated text.
pitfalls: Treating voice activity detection as proof that a semantic turn is complete
Adding overlapping latency spans as though they were serial
Speaking a factual tool result from an unstable partial transcript
Keeping unheard or cancelled audio in the conversation history
Presenting an illustrative timing trace as a production latency guarantee
